name: Budgets and Allowable Costs
title: Budgets and Allowable Costs
answer: Budgets and allowable costs in AI research grant proposals cover the direct and indirect expenses a funder will reimburse, including personnel, equipment, data acquisition, cloud compute, and institutional overhead. For AI projects, this means separating costs for data licensing, annotation labor, model training, evaluation, and storage, and showing how each line maps to the project's aims. The scope also includes budget justification narratives, cost sharing, and any caps or exclusions set by the funding program.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on institutional financial systems, grant management software, and cost accounting structures that track commitments, expenditures, and effort reporting. For AI research, the technical infrastructure being budgeted, such as high performance computing clusters, cloud GPU instances, and data repositories, is treated as a direct cost and must be matched to allowable cost categories. These systems produce the usage logs and invoices that support budget reports and audits.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Researchers and grant administrators build budgets by estimating effort, compute hours, data volume, and equipment needs, then checking each line against the funder's cost principles and the institution's negotiated indirect cost rate. They use historical rates, vendor quotes, and documented usage patterns to justify each cost as reasonable, allocable, and necessary. For AI work, the method includes separating development, training, and inference compute, and writing a budget justification that ties each cost to a specific milestone or deliverable.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Budgets are governed by funder terms and conditions, institutional policies, and audit requirements that define which costs are allowable, allocable, and reasonable. Key risks include cost disallowance, misclassification of direct and indirect costs, and unallowable expenses such as general purpose equipment without clear project justification. Provenance requires keeping receipts, timesheets, and compute usage logs to show that each cost was incurred for the project and stayed within the approved budget, and for AI work the origin of data and model assets can affect whether their acquisition costs are allowable.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Budgeting for AI research is moving toward more granular tracking of compute and data costs, with funders increasingly expecting separate line items for model training, fine-tuning, and inference. Standardized cost models for open versus closed models are emerging, along with greater attention to the environmental and energy costs of large scale compute. Allowable cost guidance is likely to evolve as data curation, model evaluation, and ongoing monitoring become recognized as distinct budget categories rather than being folded into general research support.
